4740.t: From *δημότ-ιος (-ios) with assibilation of *τ > σ, from δημότης (dēmótēs, “one of the people; fellow citizen”) + -ιος (-ios).

4750.t: From διαφαίνω (dĭăphaínō, “to shine; to be manifest”) + -ής (-ḗs, adjectival suffix).

4794.t: From Proto-Indo-European *yes- (“to boil, foam”). Compare Sanskrit येषति (yeṣati, “to boil, bubble up”), यसति (yásati, “to froth up, foam”), English yeast.

4731.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gew- (“to curve, to bend”), the same source as Old Armenian կոր (kor), Lithuanian gur̃nas (“ankle, hip, bone”), and Norwegian kaure (“curly lock of hair”). See also γυῖον (guîon, “hand; limbs”).

4732.t: From δανείζω (dăneízō, “to lend money”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

4779.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eurús, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wérus (“wide”). Compare Sanskrit उ॒रु (urú, “wide; large; spacious”) and Avestan 𐬬𐬊𐬎𐬭𐬎 (voᵘru, “wide”).

4729.t: Perhaps originally "privilege of age", from Proto-Indo-European *ǵerh₂- (“to grow old”). Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀐𐀨 (ke-ra).

4739.t: Unknown, with Beekes suspecting Pre-Greek origin.

4764.t: From δάκνω (dáknō, “to bite”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

4786.t: From εὐ- (eu-, “good”) + ζώνη (zṓnē, “belt, girdle”) and the suffix -ος (-os).

4720.t: From unattested *γέραρ, parallel form of γέρας n (géras, “gift, reward”). Morphologically, stem γερ- + -αρός (-arós).

4718.t: From Latin gaesum, itself from Gaulish *gaisos, from Proto-Celtic *gaisos (“spear”). Compare also χαῖος (khaîos, “shepherd's staff”), Sanskrit हेषस् (héṣas, “missile”).

4759.t: From δέρω (dérō, “to skin, to flay”) + -α (-ā, “nominal suffix”).
